shop.optional: Small pill badge next to a build shop category title. Marks a category as optional. Keep short, about 8 characters.
shop.imbue: Label on an item card for an item that can be imbued onto an ability. Imbue is a Deadlock game term, match the game's translation. Keep short, about 8 characters.
shop.removed_item: Name shown for a build item that no longer exists in the shop. Used as a drag label in the build editor. Keep short.
shop.description: Screen reader label for the small "more" button that shows a category's description in a tooltip.

mine.title: Option label in the Mine tab's view switch on the Builds page. Lists the user's own builds. Keep short, about 10 characters.
mine.loading: Empty state text shown while the user's own builds load, on the Builds page Mine tab.
mine.load_failed: Error message in an empty state on the Builds page Mine tab when the user's builds fail to load. Fallback text.
mine.retry: Button under the load error on the Mine tab. Reloads the user's builds. Keep short, about 9 characters.
mine.empty: Empty state text on the Mine tab when the user has no builds at all.
mine.published_failed: Warning text on the Mine tab. Published builds could not be fetched from the Deadlock API. Deadlock is the game name, keep untranslated.
mine.queue_banner: Banner on the Mine tab. Builds edited while the game runs are saved after it closes. {count} = number of waiting builds, e.g. 2. Plural forms. Deadlock stays untranslated.
mine.group_new: Group heading on the Mine tab for builds not tied to a hero yet.
mine.unknown_hero: Group heading on the Mine tab when a build's hero cannot be found. Hero is a Deadlock game term.

status.draft: Status badge on a build row, for a build with unsaved local changes. Keep short, about 5 characters.
status.waiting: Status badge on a build row. Its changes are queued and save once the game closes. Deadlock stays untranslated. Keep short, about 25 characters.
status.local: Status badge on a build row, for a build stored only in the game's local files. Keep short, about 5 characters.
status.public: Status badge on a build row, for a build published for everyone. Keep short, about 6 characters.

mine.updated: Small text on a build row. {date} = date or relative time of the last update, e.g. "3 days ago".
mine.edited: Note on a build row after the user edited it in the app. First sentence of a pair, followed by the next string. Publish is the game's own button, match the game.
mine.edited_hint: Second sentence of the note on an edited build row. Warns that the edit is lost if another build of the same hero is used first. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
mine.copy: Button on a build detail page and build row. Makes a new editable copy of the build. Keep short, about 12 characters.
mine.copy_name: Name given to a copied build. {name} = original build name, e.g. "Haze Burst".
mine.copied: Toast body shown after a build was copied.
mine.favourite: Button on a build detail page and build row. Adds the build to favourites. Keep short, about 10 characters.
mine.favourited: Toast body shown after a build was added to favourites.
mine.unfavourited: Toast body shown after a build was removed from favourites.
mine.cancel_queued: Button on a build row. Cancels a save that waits for the game to close. Keep short, about 20 characters.
mine.delete: Button on a build row. Opens a confirmation to delete the build. Keep short, about 8 characters.
mine.delete_in_game: Text on a build row where deleting is not possible from the app. The user must delete it inside the game. Keep short, about 18 characters.
mine.delete_title: Confirmation dialog title for deleting a build. {name} = build name, e.g. "Haze Burst".
mine.delete_description: Confirmation dialog body for deleting a build. The build is removed from the user's builds in the game.
mine.deleted: Toast body shown after a build was deleted.
mine.queued: Toast or inline notice on a build detail page. The change is queued and saves when the game closes. Deadlock stays untranslated.
mine.changed_in_game: Error message on a build detail page. The build changed in the game while the user acted. Asks to try again.
mine.action_failed: Fallback error message when changing a build (favourite, copy, discard) fails.
mine.flush_failed: Error toast shown when queued builds could not be written to the game after it closed.

conflict.title: Dialog title when a build was changed by the game and by the user. Deadlock stays untranslated.
conflict.description: Dialog body of the build conflict dialog, when a queued save hit a changed build. {name} = build name, e.g. "Haze Burst".
conflict.description_now: Dialog body of the build conflict dialog, when the build changed while the user was editing. {name} = build name, e.g. "Haze Burst".
conflict.mine: Column heading in the build conflict dialog for the user's own version. Keep short, about 8 characters.
conflict.game: Column heading in the build conflict dialog for the version stored by the game. Keep short, about 12 characters.
conflict.deleted: Text in the build conflict dialog when one side deleted the build. Keep short, about 10 characters.
conflict.keep_mine: Button in the build conflict dialog. Keeps the user's version. Keep short, about 12 characters.
conflict.keep_game: Button in the build conflict dialog. Keeps the game's version. Keep short, about 16 characters.

mine.draft_of: Text on a draft build row. {name} = name of the build the draft belongs to, e.g. "Haze Burst".
mine.discard_draft: Button on a build detail page. Throws away unsaved changes. Keep short, about 14 characters.
mine.draft_discarded: Toast body shown after a draft was discarded.
mine.discard_title: Confirmation dialog title for discarding a draft. {name} = build name, e.g. "Haze Burst".
mine.discard_description: Confirmation dialog body for discarding a draft. Explains the unsaved changes are lost.
mine.favourites_title: Option label in the Mine tab's view switch. Lists favourited builds. Keep short, about 10 characters.
mine.favourite_version: Part of a favourite build's info line. {version} = build version number, e.g. 4.
mine.all_heroes: Option in the hero filter dropdown on the Mine tab. Shows builds of every hero. Hero is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 10 characters.
mine.show: Label of the view switch on the Mine tab. Picks between own builds and favourites. Keep short, about 6 characters.
mine.empty_hero: Empty state text on the Mine tab when the hero filter is set. {hero} = hero name, e.g. "Haze". Hero is a Deadlock game term.
mine.favourites_empty: Empty state text on the Mine tab favourites view with no favourites.
mine.favourites_empty_hero: Empty state text on the favourites view when a hero filter is set. {hero} = hero name, e.g. "Haze". Hero is a Deadlock game term.
mine.sort_name: Sort option label in a dropdown on the Mine tab. Sorts builds by name. Keep short, about 6 characters.
mine.sort_win_rate: Sort option label in a dropdown on the Mine tab. Sorts builds by highest win rate. Keep short, about 14 characters.
mine.status_all: Option in the status filter dropdown on the Mine tab. Shows builds of any status. Keep short, about 12 characters.
mine.status_label: Screen reader label and field label of the status filter dropdown on the Mine tab. Keep short.
mine.author_any: Option in the author filter dropdown. Shows builds from any author. Keep short, about 12 characters.

browser.title: Page heading of the Builds page.
browser.subtitle: Subtitle under the Builds page heading.
browser.tab_public: Tab on the Builds page that lists public builds. Keep short, about 8 characters.
browser.tab_mine: Tab on the Builds page that lists the user's own builds. Keep short, about 6 characters.
browser.hero: Placeholder and screen reader label of the hero filter dropdown in the public builds browser. Hero is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 6 characters.
browser.sort: Screen reader label and field label of the sort dropdown in the public builds browser.
browser.sort_weekly: Sort option in the public builds browser. Orders builds by most used this week. Keep short, about 14 characters.
browser.search: Placeholder text in the search input of the public builds browser. Searches by build name.
browser.search_label: Screen reader label of the build search input.
browser.loading: Empty state text while public builds load.
browser.empty: Empty state text in the public builds browser. {hero} = hero name, e.g. "Haze". Hero is a Deadlock game term.
browser.error: Fallback error message when public builds fail to load.
browser.retry: Button under the load error in the public builds browser. Reloads the list. Keep short, about 9 characters.
browser.by: Byline on a build card. {name} = author's player name, e.g. "Sammi".
browser.updated: Small text on a build card. {date} = date or relative time of the last update, e.g. "3 days ago".
browser.this_week: Stat on a build card. {count} = number of players using the build this week, formatted, e.g. "1,200".
browser.favorites: Stat on a build card. {count} = number of favourites, formatted, e.g. "34". Plural forms.
browser.sort_popular: Sort option in the public builds browser. Orders builds by popularity. Keep short, about 10 characters.
browser.sort_favorites: Sort option. Orders builds by number of favourites. Keep short, about 15 characters.
browser.sort_updated: Sort option. Orders builds by last update time. Keep short, about 16 characters.
browser.sort_published: Sort option in the public builds browser. Orders builds by publish date. Keep short, about 18 characters.
browser.sort_versions: Sort option. Orders builds by number of versions. Keep short, about 13 characters.
browser.updated_within: Label of the dropdown that filters builds by last update time.
browser.updated_day: Option in the updated within dropdown. Builds updated in the last day. Keep short, about 5 characters.
browser.updated_week: Option in the updated within dropdown. Builds updated in the last 7 days. Keep short, about 7 characters.
browser.updated_month: Option in the updated within dropdown. Builds updated in the last 30 days. Keep short, about 7 characters.
browser.updated_all: Option in the updated within dropdown. No time limit. Keep short, about 8 characters.
browser.filters: Screen reader label for the group of filter controls in the public builds browser.
browser.tag: Screen reader label of the tag filter dropdown and of the tag list on a build card. A tag is a category label on a build.
browser.tag_any: Option in the tag filter dropdown. Shows builds with any tag. Keep short, about 8 characters.
browser.language: Label of the build language filter dropdown. Keep short, about 8 characters.
browser.language_default: Option in the build language filter. Shows builds in the app language and English.
browser.language_any: Option in the build language filter. Shows builds in every language. Keep short, about 12 characters.
browser.min_favorites: Screen reader label of the minimum favourites dropdown.
browser.favorites_any: Option in the minimum favourites dropdown. No minimum. Keep short, about 14 characters.
browser.favorites_min: Option in the minimum favourites dropdown. {count} = minimum number of favourites, e.g. 10.
browser.author: Placeholder text in the author filter input. The user types a player name or a Steam ID. Steam is a brand name.
browser.author_label: Screen reader label of the author filter input.
browser.author_clear: Tooltip and screen reader label of the button that clears the author filter.
browser.author_none: Message in the author search results list when no player matches.
browser.clear_filters: Button in the public builds browser. Resets all filters. Keep short, about 13 characters.
browser.empty_filtered: Empty state text when filters hide all public builds.
browser.win_rate: Stat on a build card. {rate} = win rate percentage, e.g. "54.2%".
browser.win_rate_detail: Tooltip on the win rate stat. {wins} = wins, e.g. 120. {matches} = matches played, e.g. 230. The period is the last 30 days.

view.back: Back link at the top of a single build page. Returns to the Builds page. Keep short, about 6 characters.
view.empty: Empty state on the single build page when no build was chosen.
view.loading: Empty state text while a single build loads.
view.load_failed: Fallback error message when a single build fails to load.
view.missing: Empty state text on the single build page when the build does not exist.
view.by_you: Byline on a build card or page for a build the user made. Keep short, about 6 characters.
view.favourited: Badge in the header of a build page for a build the user favourited. Keep short, about 18 characters.
view.open_copy: Button on a build page that opens the user's own copy of the build. Keep short, about 10 characters.
view.copy_failed: Fallback error message when copying a build fails.
view.shop: Section heading and screen reader label of the shop panel on a build page. The shop is the in game item shop, a Deadlock game term.
view.cost: Text under the shop heading on a build page. {souls} = total Soul cost, e.g. "12,400". {count} = number of items, e.g. 8. Souls is a Deadlock game term. Plural forms.
view.cost_optional: Small note next to the total cost. Optional shop categories are left out of the total.
view.removed: Notice on a build page. {count} = number of items that were removed from the game's shop, e.g. 2. Plural forms.
view.shop_failed: Empty state error in the shop panel on a build page when shop items fail to load.
view.resolution: Label of the screen resolution dropdown in the shop panel. Changes how the shop layout is previewed. Keep short, about 10 characters.
view.actual_size: Button label in the shop panel. Shows the shop at real pixel size. Keep short, about 11 characters.
view.unmeasured: Warning badge in the shop panel when the chosen resolution is not measured. Keep short, about 10 characters.
view.unmeasured_hint: Tooltip on the Unmeasured badge. 1440p is a screen resolution, keep as is.
view.abilities: Section heading of the ability order panel on a build page. Ability is a Deadlock game term.
view.no_abilities: Empty state text in the ability order panel.
view.warning_unknown_ability: Warning in a list of build problems. Ability is a Deadlock game term. The hero is a Deadlock game term.
view.warning_free_unlock: Warning in a list of build problems. Some ability unlocks in the build have no cost saved.
view.warning_ultimate_early: Warning in a list of build problems. Ultimate is a Deadlock game term, match the game's translation. The other 3 are the hero's other abilities.
view.warning_leftover: Warning in a list of build problems. The ability order has more steps than the hero can take. Ability is a Deadlock game term.
view.warning_invalid: Warning in a list of build problems. The ability order has steps the game's rules do not allow.
view.differs: Warning on a shop category. The layout shows a different column count on the user's screen. {count} = columns on this screen, e.g. 4. {reference} = columns in the game reference, e.g. 5. Plural forms.
view.category_fallback: Name for a build category without a name. {n} = position number, e.g. 2.

editor.canvas: Screen reader label for the build editor canvas that holds the shop categories and items.
editor.drag_copy: Small badge on the drag preview when dragging copies items. Keep short, about 6 characters.
editor.drag_items: Drag preview label when dragging several items. {count} = number of items, e.g. 3. Plural forms.
editor.unnamed: Drag preview label for a category without a name. Keep short, about 8 characters.
editor.rename: Screen reader label of the input used to rename a category in the build editor.
editor.size_tag: Size tag on a category in the build editor. {columns} = column count, e.g. 4. {rows} = row count, e.g. 2. The x stands for by. Keep short, about 7 characters.
editor.size_hint: Tooltip on the category size tag. Explains resizing by dragging an edge. Alt is a keyboard key name, match the keyboard.
editor.unsafe_width: Tooltip warning on a category size tag in the build editor. The category width may lose a column at another screen resolution or in the Build Browser preview.
editor.row_wraps: Tooltip warning on a category in the build editor. The row wraps at another resolution.
editor.copies: Small badge on an item in the build editor. {count} = how many times the item is in the build, e.g. 2. The x stands for times. Keep short, about 3 characters.
editor.copies_hint: Tooltip on the copies badge. {count} = how many times the item is in the build, e.g. 2. Plural forms.
editor.overflow: Badge on a category in the build editor. Its items need more height than the box has. Keep short, about 20 characters.
editor.resize_width: Screen reader label of the drag handle on a category's right edge. Keep short.
editor.resize_height: Screen reader label of the drag handle on a category's bottom edge. Keep short.
editor.resize_both: Screen reader label of the drag handle on a category's corner. Keep short.
editor.new_category: Default name for a category the user just added in the build editor.

menu.rename: Menu item in the category context menu. Renames the category. Keep short, about 8 characters.
menu.description: Menu item in the category context menu. Opens the description editor. The three dots mean more input follows. Keep short, about 14 characters.
menu.optional: Checkbox menu item in the category context menu. Marks the category as optional. Keep short, about 10 characters.
menu.fit_to_items: Menu item in the category context menu. Resizes the category to fit its items. Keep short, about 13 characters.
menu.fill_row: Menu item in the category context menu. Stretches the category across the row. Keep short, about 10 characters.
menu.set_size: Menu item in the category context menu. Opens the size dialog. The three dots mean a dialog follows. Keep short, about 12 characters.
menu.copy_size: Menu item in the category context menu. Copies the category's size. Keep short, about 10 characters.
menu.paste_size: Menu item in the category context menu. Applies a copied size. Keep short, about 11 characters.
menu.row: Submenu title in the category context menu for row wide actions. Keep short, about 4 characters.
menu.equal_widths: Menu item in the Row submenu. Gives all categories in the row the same width. Keep short, about 13 characters.
menu.equal_rows: Menu item in the Row submenu. Gives all categories in the row the same row count. Keep short, about 11 characters.
menu.equalize_heights: Menu item in the Row submenu. Gives all categories in the row the same height. Keep short, about 17 characters.
menu.fill_row_proportionally: Menu item in the Row submenu. Stretches categories across the row, keeping their width ratio. Keep short, about 24 characters.
menu.duplicate: Menu item in the category context menu. Makes a copy of the category. Keep short, about 10 characters.
menu.split_in_half: Menu item in the category context menu. Splits the category into two. Keep short, about 13 characters.
menu.merge_with_next: Menu item in the category context menu. Joins the category with the next one. Keep short, about 16 characters.
menu.sort_items: Menu item in the category context menu. Sorts the items in the category. Keep short, about 10 characters.
menu.remove: Menu item in the category context menu. Opens a confirmation to remove the category. Keep short, about 8 characters.
menu.remove_title: Confirmation dialog title for removing a category. {name} = category name, e.g. "Early game".
menu.remove_description: Confirmation dialog body for removing a category. {count} = number of items in it, e.g. 6.
menu.cancel: Cancel button of the remove category confirmation dialog. Keep short, about 6 characters.
menu.apply: Button in the set size dialog. Applies the new size. Keep short, about 6 characters.
menu.unnamed: Fallback category name used in menus and dialogs when a category has no name. Keep short, about 8 characters.
menu.category_actions: Screen reader label of the button that opens a category's context menu. {name} = category name, e.g. "Early game".
menu.set_size_title: Title of the set size dialog for a category.
menu.columns: Field label in the set size dialog for the column count. Keep short, about 8 characters.
menu.rows: Field label in the set size dialog for the row count. Keep short, about 5 characters.
menu.decrease: Screen reader label of a minus button in the set size dialog. {label} = field name, e.g. "Columns" (lowercase may be needed).
menu.increase: Screen reader label of a plus button in the set size dialog. {label} = field name, e.g. "Columns" (lowercase may be needed).
menu.size_range: Hint text in the set size dialog. {max} = highest allowed column count, e.g. 6.
menu.name: Field label of the category name input in the editor side panel. Keep short, about 6 characters.
menu.description_label: Field label of the category description input in the editor side panel. Keep short, about 12 characters.
menu.note: Menu item in the item context menu. Opens the item note editor. The three dots mean more input follows. Keep short, about 8 characters.
menu.sell_priority: Menu item in the item context menu. Opens the sell priority setting. Keep short, about 16 characters.
menu.imbue_target: Menu item in the item context menu. Picks which ability the item is imbued onto. Imbue and ability are Deadlock game terms. Keep short, about 16 characters.
menu.flex_slots: Menu item in the item context menu. Sets how many flex slots the item needs. Flex slot is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 22 characters.
menu.move_to: Submenu title in the item side panel. Moves the item to another category. Keep short, about 18 characters.
menu.swap_with: Submenu title in the item side panel. Replaces the item with a related item. Keep short, about 10 characters.
menu.upgrades: Group heading in the swap submenu for upgrade items. Item is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 10 characters.
menu.components: Group heading in the swap submenu for component items. Item is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 12 characters.
menu.split_here: Menu item in the item context menu. Splits the category at this item. Keep short, about 19 characters.
menu.item_title: Fallback title of the item section in the editor side panel when the item name is unknown. Keep short.
menu.note_label: Field label of the item note input in the editor side panel. Keep short, about 6 characters.
menu.imbue_label: Field label of the imbue target dropdown in the editor side panel. Imbue is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 14 characters.
menu.imbue_none: Option in the imbue target dropdown. No target chosen. Keep short, about 6 characters.
menu.sell_label: Field label of the sell priority input in the editor side panel. Keep short, about 14 characters.
menu.flex_label: Field label of the flex slots input in the editor side panel. Flex slot is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 20 characters.
menu.whole_number: Validation error under a number input in the editor side panel.

picker.label: Screen reader label of the item shop flyout in the build editor. Item shop is a Deadlock game term.
picker.search: Placeholder text in the item search input of the shop flyout. Items can be searched by name or stat.
picker.search_label: Screen reader label of the item search input in the shop flyout.
picker.slot_weapon: Tab in the shop flyout for the Weapon item category. Weapon is a Deadlock game term, match the game's translation. Keep short, about 8 characters.
picker.slot_vitality: Tab in the shop flyout for the Vitality item category. Vitality is a Deadlock game term, match the game's translation. Keep short, about 9 characters.
picker.slot_spirit: Tab in the shop flyout for the Spirit item category. Spirit is a Deadlock game term, match the game's translation. Keep short, about 7 characters.
picker.tier: Small text on an item in the editor side panel. {tier} = item tier number, e.g. 3. Tier is a Deadlock game term.
picker.count: Small badge on an item chip showing how many copies. {count} = number of copies, e.g. 2. The x stands for times. Keep short, about 3 characters.
picker.add: Screen reader label of an item tile in the shop flyout. {name} = item name, e.g. "Mystic Burst". Item is a Deadlock game term.
picker.add_counted: Screen reader label of an item tile already in the build. {name} = item name, e.g. "Mystic Burst". {count} = copies already in the build, e.g. 2.
picker.no_results: Empty state text in the shop flyout when a search finds nothing. {query} = the user's search text, e.g. "burst".
picker.empty: Empty state error in the shop flyout when the shop items fail to load.
picker.phase_early: Option in the game phase dropdown of the shop flyout. Shows items popular in the early game. Keep short, about 10 characters.
picker.phase_mid: Option in the game phase dropdown of the shop flyout. Shows items popular in the mid game. Keep short, about 9 characters.
picker.phase_late: Option in the Game phase dropdown of the build editor's item shop panel. Filters items to the late stage of a match. Keep short, about 10 characters.

abilities.title: Heading of the ability order bar at the bottom of the build editor. The order in which hero abilities get upgraded.
abilities.no_kit: Empty state in the ability order bar of the build editor, shown when the hero's ability data could not be loaded.
abilities.ultimate: Tooltip and screen reader label on a star badge over a hero's ultimate ability icon in the ability order bar. Ultimate is a Deadlock game term.
abilities.unlock: Part of a tooltip on an ability icon in the ability order bar. Names the step that first unlocks the ability, before any tier upgrade.
abilities.unlock_short: Tiny uppercase label on a step chip in the ability order sequence. Marks a step that unlocks an ability. Keep short, about 6 characters.
abilities.tier: Part of a tooltip on an ability icon in the ability order bar. Names an upgrade tier. {tier} = tier number, e.g. 2.
abilities.level: Small label on a step chip in the ability order sequence. {level} = hero level, e.g. 5. Keep short, about 6 characters.
abilities.remove_hint: Tooltip line on a step in the ability order bar telling the user a click removes that step. {step} = step number, e.g. 3.
abilities.also_removes: Tooltip line in the ability order bar. Removing a step also removes later steps. {count} = number of later steps, e.g. 2. {steps} = list of step numbers, e.g. "#4, #5".
abilities.reason_locked: Tooltip on a disabled ability icon in the ability order bar. Says why it cannot be added yet.
abilities.reason_tier_order: Tooltip on a disabled ability icon in the ability order bar. Says why the next tier cannot be added yet. Tiers are ability upgrade levels.
abilities.reason_ultimate: Tooltip on the disabled ultimate ability icon in the ability order bar. Ultimate is a Deadlock game term.
abilities.reason_maxed: Tooltip on a disabled ability icon in the ability order bar. Says the ability has no more tiers to add.
abilities.reason_unknown: Tooltip on a disabled ability icon in the ability order bar. Says the ability does not belong to the selected hero.
abilities.sequence: Screen reader label for the scrolling row of ordered steps in the ability order bar.
abilities.sequence_hint: Hint text in the ability order bar telling how to reorder steps. Drag, or press Alt with the Left and Right arrow keys. Keep the key names understandable.
abilities.chip_label: Screen reader label for one step chip in the ability order sequence. {step} = step number, e.g. 2. {ability} = ability name, e.g. "Heat Wave". {kind} = Unlock or tier text, e.g. "Tier 2".
abilities.clear: Small button in the ability order bar that removes all steps. Keep short, about 5 characters.
abilities.spent: Status text in the ability order bar. {spent} = ability points used so far, e.g. 4. AP means ability points.
abilities.spent_of: Status text in the ability order bar. {spent} = ability points used, e.g. 4. {available} = points available at this point, e.g. 6. AP means ability points.
abilities.last_level: Status text in the ability order bar. {level} = hero level at which the last step becomes affordable, e.g. 9.
abilities.last_level_unknown: Status text in the ability order bar, shown when the level of the last step cannot be worked out.
abilities.dropped: Notice in the ability order bar after loading a saved build, plural. {count} = number of saved steps that were left out, e.g. 2.
abilities.moved: Notice in the ability order bar after loading a saved build, plural. {count} = number of steps moved later, e.g. 2.
abilities.clean_up: Small button next to a notice in the ability order bar. Fixes the order automatically. Keep short, about 8 characters.
abilities.adds: Tooltip line on an ability icon in the ability order bar. {kind} = Unlock or tier text, e.g. "Tier 2". {step} = step number it will take, e.g. 4.
abilities.adds_at: Tooltip line on an ability icon in the ability order bar. {kind} = Unlock or tier text, e.g. "Tier 2". {step} = step number, e.g. 4. {level} = hero level, e.g. 6.
abilities.right_click_removes: Tooltip line on an ability icon in the ability order bar. A right click removes the last step. {step} = step number, e.g. 3.
abilities.remove_step: Screen reader label for the button that removes one step in the ability order bar. {step} = step number, e.g. 3.
abilities.empty_bar: Empty state in the ability order bar telling the user to click an ability icon to begin the order.
abilities.icons_label: Screen reader label for the group of hero ability icons in the ability order bar.
abilities.step_kind: Tooltip line for a step in the ability order sequence. {step} = step number, e.g. 2. {kind} = Unlock or tier text, e.g. "Tier 2".
abilities.step_level: Tooltip line for a step in the ability order sequence. {level} = hero level, e.g. 6. {souls} = souls needed, e.g. 3,400. Souls is a Deadlock game term.
abilities.step_level_unknown: Tooltip line for a step in the ability order sequence. Says the step comes after the last known hero level.
abilities.cost_unlock: Tooltip line for a step in the ability order sequence. Says the step uses one ability unlock.
abilities.cost_points: Tooltip line for a step in the ability order sequence. {points} = ability points used, e.g. 2. AP means ability points.
abilities.final_locked: Tooltip line on an ability icon in the ability order bar. Says the ability is never unlocked by the current order.
abilities.final_unlocked: Tooltip line on an ability icon in the ability order bar. {step} = step number where it unlocks, e.g. 3.
abilities.final_tier: Tooltip line on an ability icon in the ability order bar. {tier} = highest tier reached, e.g. 2. {step} = step number, e.g. 7.
abilities.unlocks_first: Small button in the ability order bar that moves all unlock steps to the front. Keep short, about 14 characters.
abilities.unlocks_first_hint: Tooltip on the Unlocks first button in the ability order bar. Deadlock is the game and stays untranslated.

details.name: Field label above the build name input in the build editor's side panel. Names the build.
details.description: Field label above the build description input in the build editor's side panel.
details.description_too_long: Warning under the build description input in the build editor when the text is over the game's limit.
details.publish_needs: Hint in the build editor's side panel. Says the game needs both a name and a description before a build can be published.
details.language: Field label for the build language dropdown in the build editor's side panel.
details.language_unknown: Fallback option text in the build language dropdown when the language is not recognised. {id} = numeric language id, e.g. 7.
details.tags: Field label for the build tags in the build editor's side panel. Tags are short labels shown on a build.
details.tags_standard: Group heading inside the tag picker menu in the build editor. Lists the game's standard tags.
details.tags_abilities: Group heading inside the tag picker menu in the build editor. Lists the hero's ability tags. Ability is a Deadlock game term.
details.tags_items: Submenu title inside the tag picker menu in the build editor. Opens a list of items used in the build. Item is a Deadlock game term.
details.tag_remove: Screen reader label for a button that removes a tag from the build. {name} = tag name, e.g. "Melee".
details.tag_unknown: Fallback label for a build tag the app does not recognise. {id} = numeric tag id, e.g. 12.
details.tag_weapon: Standard build tag name in the tag picker and on a build. Weapon is a Deadlock item category and should match the game's own translation.
details.tag_vitality: Standard build tag name in the tag picker and on a build. Vitality is a Deadlock item category and should match the game's own translation.
details.tag_spirit: Standard build tag name in the tag picker and on a build. Spirit is a Deadlock item category and should match the game's own translation.
details.tag_complexity_1: Standard build tag name. Marks a build as suited to beginners. Should match the game's own translation.
details.tag_complexity_2: Standard build tag name. Marks a build as suited to players with some experience. Should match the game's own translation.
details.tag_complexity_3: Standard build tag name. Marks a build as suited to expert players. Should match the game's own translation.
details.tag_damage: Standard build tag name. Marks a build focused on dealing damage. Should match the game's own translation.
details.tag_utility: Standard build tag name. Marks a build focused on utility. Should match the game's own translation.
details.tag_healing: Standard build tag name. Marks a build focused on healing. Should match the game's own translation.
details.tag_crowd_control: Standard build tag name. Marks a build focused on crowd control. Should match the game's own translation.
details.tag_mobility: Standard build tag name. Marks a build focused on movement. Should match the game's own translation.
details.tag_melee: Standard build tag name. Marks a build focused on melee attacks. Should match the game's own translation.
details.tag_headshots: Standard build tag name. Marks a build focused on headshots. Should match the game's own translation.
details.tag_debuff: Standard build tag name. Marks a build focused on debuffs. Should match the game's own translation.
details.support: Setting label next to a toggle in the build editor's side panel. When on, a credit line for Deadlock+ is added to the build description. Deadlock+ stays untranslated.
details.support_footer: Credit line added under a build's description in the game when the support toggle is on. {url} = website address, e.g. "deadlockplus.app". Deadlock+ stays untranslated.

editor.edit: Button on a build's detail view that opens the build in the editor. The build is the user's own. Keep short, about 4 characters.
editor.edit_copy: Button on a build's detail view that opens a copy of someone else's build in the editor. Keep short, about 12 characters.
editor.new_build: Button that starts a new empty build in the build editor. Keep short, about 9 characters.
editor.back: Button with a back arrow at the top of the build editor page. Returns to the builds list. Keep short, about 14 characters.
editor.first_category: Default name given to the first category of a new build. A category is a titled group of items in a build.
editor.name_placeholder: Placeholder text in the build name input of the build editor.
editor.name_needed: Hint in the build editor shown when the build has no name yet. Says a name is needed before saving.
editor.undo: Screen reader label for the undo icon button in the build editor toolbar.
editor.undo_tooltip: Tooltip on the undo icon button in the build editor toolbar. The keyboard shortcut in brackets stays as is.
editor.redo: Screen reader label for the redo icon button in the build editor toolbar.
editor.redo_tooltip: Tooltip on the redo icon button in the build editor toolbar. The keyboard shortcut in brackets stays as is.
editor.save: Main button in the build editor toolbar. Writes the build into Deadlock's own build list. Deadlock stays untranslated. Keep short, about 14 characters.
editor.save_failed: Error toast shown when saving a build to the game fails.
editor.load_failed: Error message in the build editor page when the build could not be opened. A reason may follow.
editor.loading: Loading text in the build editor page while the build opens.
editor.missing: Empty state in the build editor page when the requested build no longer exists.
editor.catalog_failed: Error message in the build editor page when the game's item list could not be read. Item is a Deadlock game term.
editor.publish_note: Note in the build editor for a build the user already published in the game. Explains that Save keeps edits locally and publishing is done in the game. Deadlock stays untranslated.
editor.status_saved: Save status label in the build editor toolbar. The build is written to the game.
editor.status_queued: Save status label in the build editor toolbar. The save will happen when the game is closed. Deadlock stays untranslated.
editor.status_draft: Save status label in the build editor toolbar. A local draft is kept but the game has not been changed.
editor.status_unsaved: Save status label in the build editor toolbar. There are changes that are not saved anywhere yet.
editor.status_saving: Save status label in the build editor toolbar while a save is running.
editor.status_conflict: Save status label in the build editor toolbar. The build was changed in the game after the editor opened it.
editor.status_draft_failed: Save status label in the build editor toolbar when the local draft could not be saved.

history.open: Button in the build editor toolbar that opens the saved versions dialog. Keep short, about 7 characters.
history.title: Dialog title of the saved versions dialog in the build editor.
history.list: Screen reader label for the list of saved versions in the saved versions dialog.
history.load_failed: Error message in the saved versions dialog when the list of versions could not be read.
history.empty: Empty state in the saved versions dialog. A version is kept each time the build is saved to the game.
history.age_now: Relative time on a saved version row. Means the version was saved moments ago. Keep short, about 8 characters.
history.age_minutes: Relative time on a saved version row, plural. {count} = number of minutes, e.g. 5.
history.age_hours: Relative time on a saved version row, plural. {count} = number of hours, e.g. 3.
history.age_days: Relative time on a saved version row, plural. {count} = number of days, e.g. 2.
history.items: Detail on a saved version row, plural. {count} = number of items in that version, e.g. 12. Item is a Deadlock game term.
history.restore: Button in the saved versions dialog that loads the chosen version into the editor. Keep short, about 7 characters.
history.restore_note: Note next to the Restore button in the saved versions dialog. Says restoring only changes the editor, can be undone, and the game stays unchanged until saved.
history.version_failed: Error message in the saved versions dialog when one version could not be read.

timeline.label: Screen reader label for the souls timeline chart at the bottom of the build editor. Souls is a Deadlock game term.
timeline.assumption: Tooltip text on the info button of the souls timeline. Explains the timeline assumes souls are spent right away and times are hero averages. Souls is a Deadlock game term.
timeline.souls: Readout line on the souls timeline. {souls} = souls amount, e.g. 4,200. Souls is a Deadlock game term.
timeline.level: Readout line on the souls timeline. {level} = hero level, e.g. 8.
timeline.time: Readout line on the souls timeline. {time} = estimated match clock time, e.g. "12:34".
timeline.step_unlock: Readout line on the souls timeline for an ability unlock step. {name} = ability name, e.g. "Heat Wave".
timeline.step_tier: Readout line on the souls timeline for an ability upgrade step. {name} = ability name, e.g. "Heat Wave". {tier} = tier number, e.g. 2. T is short for tier. Keep short.
timeline.about: Screen reader label for the small info button next to the souls timeline.
timeline.items: Lane label on the souls timeline chart for item purchases. Item is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 5 characters.
timeline.abilities: Lane label on the souls timeline chart for ability upgrades. Ability is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 9 characters.

investment.weapon: Lane label on the souls timeline chart for weapon investment. Matches the game's stat name for weapon damage. Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 13 characters.
investment.spirit: Lane label on the souls timeline chart for spirit investment. Matches the game's stat name for spirit power. Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 12 characters.
investment.vitality: Lane label on the souls timeline chart for vitality investment. Matches the game's stat name for max health. Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 10 characters.

shop.popular: Heading and tab in the build editor's item shop panel. Lists items other players pick most for this hero. Keep short, about 7 characters.
shop.search: Heading and tab in the build editor's item shop panel for searching items. Keep short, about 6 characters.
shop.close: Screen reader label for the icon button that closes the item shop panel in the build editor.
shop.popular_loading: Loading text in the item shop panel of the build editor, on the Popular tab.
shop.popular_empty: Empty state in the item shop panel of the build editor, on the Popular tab. Item is a Deadlock game term.
shop.phase_all: Option in the Game phase dropdown of the item shop panel. Shows items from every stage of a match. Keep short, about 3 characters.
shop.phase_label: Screen reader label for the game phase dropdown in the item shop panel of the build editor.
shop.filters_label: Screen reader label for the group of filter chips in the item shop panel of the build editor.
shop.no_filter_results: Empty state in the item shop panel of the build editor when no items match the chosen filters. Item is a Deadlock game term.
shop.filter_physical: Filter chip in the item shop panel. Item category label. Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation. Keep short, about 8 characters.
shop.filter_spirit: Filter chip in the item shop panel. Item category label. Spirit is a Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation. Keep short, about 6 characters.
shop.filter_defense: Filter chip in the item shop panel. Item category label. Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation. Keep short, about 7 characters.
shop.filter_mobility: Filter chip in the item shop panel. Item category label. Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation. Keep short, about 8 characters.
shop.filter_disruption: Filter chip in the item shop panel. Item category label. Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation. Keep short, about 10 characters.
shop.filter_misc: Filter chip in the item shop panel for items that fit no other group. Short for miscellaneous. Keep short, about 4 characters.

editor.resize_label: Live label shown while dragging to resize a category in the build editor. {columns} = column count text, e.g. "4 columns". {rows} = row count text, e.g. "2 rows". The x is a multiplication sign.
editor.columns_count: Part of the resize label in the build editor, plural. {count} = number of columns, e.g. 4.
editor.rows_count: Part of the resize label in the build editor, plural. {count} = number of rows, e.g. 2.
editor.add_first_category: Button on the empty build editor canvas that adds the first category. A category is a titled group of items.
editor.empty_canvas: Empty state on the build editor canvas. Items can be dragged in from the shop to start a category. Item is a Deadlock game term.

inspector.label: Screen reader label for the side panel on the left of the build editor that shows details of the build, a category or an item.
inspector.build: Section heading in the build editor's side panel for settings of the whole build. Keep short, about 5 characters.
inspector.category: Section heading in the build editor's side panel for settings of the selected category. Keep short, about 8 characters.
inspector.item: Section heading and screen reader label in the build editor's side panel for the selected item. Item is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 4 characters.
inspector.select_category: Empty state in the build editor's side panel asking the user to pick a category on the canvas.
inspector.select_item: Empty state in the build editor's side panel asking the user to pick an item on the canvas. Item is a Deadlock game term.
inspector.items_selected: Heading in the build editor's side panel when several items are selected, plural. {count} = number of selected items, e.g. 3. Item is a Deadlock game term.
inspector.tag_slot_empty: Screen reader label for an empty tag slot button in the build editor's side panel. {slot} = slot number, e.g. 2.
inspector.tag_slot_filled: Screen reader label for a filled tag slot button in the build editor's side panel. {slot} = slot number, e.g. 2. {name} = tag name, e.g. "Melee".
inspector.tag_clear: Menu item in the tag picker of the build editor that empties the tag slot. Keep short, about 9 characters.

toolbar.label: Screen reader label for the toolbar at the top of the build editor.
toolbar.add_category: Button in the build editor toolbar that adds a category to the build. A category is a titled group of items. Keep short, about 12 characters.
toolbar.compact_all: Button in the build editor toolbar that tidies all categories into compact sizes. Keep short, about 11 characters.
toolbar.resolution: Label for the screen resolution switch in the build editor toolbar. Chooses which game screen size the canvas previews.
toolbar.resolution_hint: Tooltip on the resolution switch in the build editor toolbar. 1080p, 1440p and 4K are screen resolutions and stay as is. Build Browser is Deadlock's in game build list.
toolbar.zoom: Screen reader label for the group of zoom buttons in the build editor toolbar.
toolbar.zoom_fit: Button in the build editor toolbar that zooms the canvas to fit the window. Keep short, about 3 characters.
toolbar.zoom_in: Screen reader label for the zoom in icon button in the build editor toolbar.
toolbar.zoom_in_tooltip: Tooltip on the zoom in icon button in the build editor toolbar. The keyboard shortcut in brackets stays as is.
toolbar.zoom_out: Screen reader label for the zoom out icon button in the build editor toolbar.
toolbar.zoom_out_tooltip: Tooltip on the zoom out icon button in the build editor toolbar. The keyboard shortcut in brackets stays as is.
toolbar.snap: Screen reader label for a toggle icon button in the build editor toolbar that snaps category sizes to safe values.
toolbar.snap_tooltip: Tooltip on the snap toggle in the build editor toolbar. Safe sizes keep the same column count at every screen resolution.
toolbar.preview: Option in the build editor's resolution switch. Shows how Deadlock's Build Browser draws the build. Build Browser is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 7 characters.

editor.row_edge: Label on a divider between category rows on the build editor canvas that can be dragged to move categories to another row. Keep short, about 8 characters.
editor.row_edge_pull: Hint shown while resizing a category past the row edge in the build editor. The user should keep dragging to start a new row.
editor.row_edge_release: Hint shown while resizing a category past the row edge in the build editor. Letting go starts a new row.
editor.row_edge_pull_next: Hint shown while resizing a category in the build editor. Keep dragging to push the categories after it to a new row.
editor.row_edge_release_next: Hint shown while resizing a category in the build editor. Letting go pushes the categories after it to a new row.

layout.issues: Button label with a dropdown in the build editor toolbar, plural. {count} = number of layout problems found, e.g. 2.
layout.heading: Heading at the top of the layout issues dropdown in the build editor. Build Browser is Deadlock's in game build list. 1080p, 1440p and 4K stay as is.
layout.kind_unsized: Tooltip on a layout issue row in the build editor. The category has no stored size.
layout.kind_cap: Tooltip on a layout issue row in the build editor. The category is wider than the game can draw.
layout.kind_columns: Tooltip on a layout issue row in the build editor. At another screen resolution the category shows one column fewer.
layout.kind_row: Tooltip on a layout issue row in the build editor. At another screen resolution the category's row breaks in a different place.
layout.kind_height: Tooltip on a layout issue row in the build editor. The category is taller than the box the game gives it.
layout.fix_all: Menu item in the layout issues dropdown of the build editor that fixes every issue at once. Keep short, about 7 characters.
layout.fix_hint: Description under the Fix all menu item in the layout issues dropdown. Mentions 1440p, a screen resolution that stays as is.
layout.marker: Screen reader label and tooltip trigger for a small warning marker on a category in the build editor canvas.
layout.kind_preview_columns: Tooltip on a layout issue row in the build editor. Build Browser is Deadlock's in game build list. The category shows fewer columns there.
layout.kind_preview_row: Tooltip on a layout issue row in the build editor. Build Browser is Deadlock's in game build list. The category's row breaks differently there.
layout.kind_title_wraps: Tooltip on a layout issue row in the build editor. The category name is too long, wraps onto a second line in the game and covers items.

preview.label: Screen reader label for the canvas that previews the build as Deadlock's Build Browser shows it. Build Browser is a Deadlock game term.
preview.note: Note under the Build Browser preview canvas in the build editor. Build Browser is a Deadlock game term. The preview is a prediction.

editor.hidden_items: Badge on a category in the build editor canvas, plural. {count} = number of items that do not fit and are hidden, e.g. 2. Keep short, about 8 characters.

list.label: Screen reader label for the list of public builds on the Builds page.
list.back: Button with a back arrow on the build detail panel. Returns to the list of builds. Keep short, about 10 characters.
list.open_full: Link on the build detail panel that opens the build on its own full page. Keep short, about 14 characters.

code.copy: Button on a build's detail view that copies a build code to paste into Deadlock. Deadlock stays untranslated. Keep short, about 13 characters.
code.steps_show: Screen reader label and tooltip on a help icon button next to the copy button. Opens steps for pasting a build into Deadlock. Deadlock stays untranslated.
code.copied_title: Dialog title shown after a build code was copied to the clipboard.
code.copied_description: Line under the dialog title after copying a build code. Introduces a numbered list of steps to follow in Deadlock. Deadlock stays untranslated.
code.steps_title: Dialog title of the help dialog with numbered steps for pasting a build into Deadlock. Deadlock stays untranslated.
code.step_hero: Numbered step in the paste instructions. {hero} = hero name, e.g. "Haze". Hero is a Deadlock game term.
code.step_hero_unknown: Numbered step in the paste instructions, used when the hero is not known. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
code.step_menu: Numbered step in the paste instructions. Tells the user to open the build menu in Deadlock. Deadlock stays untranslated.
code.step_browser: Numbered step in the paste instructions. Build Browser is the name of a button in Deadlock and should match the game's own translation.
code.step_create: Numbered step in the paste instructions. Create New Build is the name of a button in Deadlock and should match the game's own translation.
code.step_paste: Numbered step in the paste instructions. Paste Build is the name of a button in Deadlock and should match the game's own translation.
code.done: Button that closes the paste instructions dialog. Keep short, about 6 characters.
code.copy_failed: Error toast shown when copying a build code to the clipboard fails.
code.paste: Button on the Builds page that opens a dialog to import a build code. Keep short, about 12 characters.
code.paste_title: Dialog title of the import build code dialog.
code.paste_description: Description in the import build code dialog. Copy build to clipboard is the name of a button in Deadlock and should match the game's own translation. Deadlock stays untranslated.
code.paste_label: Field label above the text box where a build code is pasted in the import dialog.
code.paste_submit: Submit button of the import build code dialog. Opens the pasted build in the editor. Keep short, about 14 characters.
code.import_failed: Error message in the import build code dialog when the pasted code could not be opened.

hero_stat.bullet_damage: Fallback stat name shown in an item tooltip row when the game's own text is unavailable. Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation.
hero_stat.spirit_resist: Fallback stat name shown in an item tooltip row when the game's own text is unavailable. Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation.

item_tooltip.passive: Label in an item tooltip that marks passive effects. Matches the game's own tooltip, so use the game's translation if it exists.
item_tooltip.active: Label in an item tooltip and on item cards that marks an active ability. Matches the game's own tooltip, so use the game's translation if it exists.
item_tooltip.owned: Label in an item tooltip when the player already owns the item. Use the game's own translation if it exists.
item_tooltip.imbued_upon: Line in an item tooltip. {ability} = ability name, e.g. "Rapid Fire". The item is imbued onto that ability. Ability is a Deadlock game term. Use the game's translation if it exists.
item_tooltip.upgrades_from: Heading in an item tooltip above the list of items this item is built from. Ends with a colon. Use the game's own translation if it exists.
item_tooltip.upgrades_to: Heading in an item tooltip above the list of items this item upgrades into. Ends with a colon. Use the game's own translation if it exists.
item_tooltip.used_in: Heading in an item tooltip above the list of items that use this item as a component. Ends with a colon. Use the game's own translation if it exists.
item_tooltip.popular_early: Line in an item tooltip. {percent} = percentage number, e.g. 42. Early game is the first phase of a match. Use the game's own wording if it exists.
item_tooltip.popular_mid: Line in an item tooltip. {percent} = percentage number, e.g. 42. Mid game is the middle phase of a match. Use the game's own wording if it exists.
item_tooltip.popular_late: Line in an item tooltip. {percent} = percentage number, e.g. 42. Late game is the last phase of a match. Use the game's own wording if it exists.
item_tooltip.see_details: Link or button text in an item tooltip that opens more item stats. Use the game's own translation if it exists.
item_tooltip.varies_by_hero: Note in an item tooltip. The value depends on which hero uses the item. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
item_tooltip.phase_heading: Section heading in an item tooltip above stats per game phase. Deadlock+ stays untranslated.
item_tooltip.phase_early: Row label in an item tooltip stats section. Early phase of a match. Keep short, about 10 characters.
item_tooltip.phase_mid: Row label in an item tooltip stats section. Middle phase of a match. Keep short, about 8 characters.
item_tooltip.phase_late: Row label in an item tooltip stats section. Last phase of a match. Keep short, about 9 characters.
item_tooltip.phase_rates: Row value in an item tooltip stats section. {pick} = pick rate percentage, e.g. 35. {win} = win rate percentage, e.g. 52.
item_tooltip.sell_priority: Line in an item tooltip. {priority} = a priority level text, e.g. "High". Use the game's own translation if it exists.
item_tooltip.imbue_suggestion: Heading in an item tooltip above a suggested ability to imbue this item onto. Ends with a colon. Use the game's own translation if it exists.
item_tooltip.modifies: Label in an item tooltip for the ability the item modifies. Use the game's own translation if it exists.

ability_tooltip.imbued_by: Line in an ability tooltip. {item} = item name, e.g. "Mystic Reach". That item is imbued on this ability. Use the game's own translation if it exists.
ability_tooltip.recommended: Badge in an ability tooltip next to the suggested upgrade tier. Use the game's own translation if it exists. Keep short, about 11 characters.
ability_tooltip.status_effect: Label in an ability tooltip that marks a status effect. Use the game's own translation if it exists.

item_card.new: Small badge on an item card in the shop for newly added items. Keep short, about 3 characters.
